name: John Hickenlooper

summary.text: John Hickenlooper is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from Colorado, in office since January 2021 and seeking a second term; he previously served as governor of Colorado (2011-2019) and mayor of Denver (2003-2011).
Before entering politics he worked in petroleum geology and founded a brewpub.
He was born in Narberth, Pennsylvania, in 1952 and holds a bachelor's and a master's degree in geology from Wesleyan University.

experience.text: U.S. Senator from Colorado, January 2021-present; sits on the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Energy and Natural Resources; Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; and Small Business and Entrepreneurship committees.
Bachelor's degree (1974) and master's degree (1980) in geology from Wesleyan University.
Career experience includes working with Buckhorn Petroleum and founding a brewpub.

record.detail: Voted Nay on final Senate passage; the bill passed 50-50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.

record.title: S. 5, Laken Riley Act, final Senate passage
record.detail: Voted Nay on final Senate passage; the bill, which requires federal detention of certain unauthorized immigrants charged with theft and other offenses, passed 64-35.

record.detail: Authored and voted Yea on his own amendment to modify the provision terminating the residential clean-energy tax credit; the amendment was rejected 48-52.

record.title: S.Amdt. 2107 to H.Con.Res. 14 (Hickenlooper Amendment)
record.detail: Authored and voted Yea on his own amendment to prevent using proceeds from federal public-land sales to reduce the deficit; the amendment was rejected 48-51.

record.detail: Voted Yea. The motion was agreed to 65-33. The bill became Public Law 117-159 on June 25, 2022.

positions.note: Voted to terminate the national emergency used to impose broad global tariffs, i.e. against keeping those tariffs. In an Oct. 5, 2026 Colorado Sun questionnaire he said directly, 'No. I think the tariffs have been a significant drag on our economy and have been especially harmful to ranchers and farmers across the country,' but the recorded vote is used here per source-strength ranking.

research_notes: Hickenlooper had not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey as of this research. No sourced statement was found addressing most 2026 Colorado ballot measures (Amendments 81-87, Propositions NN and 132-137), housing-state-zoning, or immigration-notify-ice specifically, so those are left unknown rather than inferred from general rhetoric. Where both an official recorded vote/sponsored amendment and looser campaign-site language existed for the same statement (keep-tariffs, deportation-priority), the recorded vote was used per the protocol's source-strength ranking, which yields a value of 2 rather than the more extreme value his campaign rhetoric alone might suggest; a reviewer may want to weigh the stronger direct-statement language too. Campaign-site quotes (hickenlooper.com/issues/) are undated on the page itself; dated here as of the 2026-10-14 access date. Second pass 2026-10-14: checked the Denver Post's Oct. 3, 2026 Senate candidate Q&A and the Colorado Sun's Oct. 11, 2026 debate recap; both reinforce statements already sourced above (federal-budget-law, keep-tariffs, clean-energy-shift, public-lands, deportation-priority) without adding a new one, and neither addresses housing-state-zoning, immigration-notify-ice, or the outstanding ballot measures, so no positions were added.
